title: L2 · NEWSROOM · Insider sale: divide, don't read · 2026-09-25 · for marketing review [STOCK]
x: A Form 4 landed at the SEC after Thursday's closing bell. Robinhood's CEO sold about $30.2m of $HOOD. One line in it says his direct holding of those shares is now zero. That is the headline everyone will read. It's the wrong number. Here's the right one.

The filing, in plain words. On 22 Sep he converted 240,834 Class B shares into Class A and sold every one. Two prints: a weighted average of $125.33 and one of $126.14. Proceeds about $30.2m. Direct Class A shares held after the sales: 0.

Now the next line. Class B shares still held after the conversion: 47,794,572. Divide 240,834 by that. 0.50%. Half of one percent of his stake. That's the whole sale. Look at the chart on post 1. The red sliver is what he sold. The navy bar is what he kept.

One more line, and it's the one that matters. The sale was made under a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted on 5 September 2025. A year-old calendar. He set the date long before he knew the price. That's not a verdict on the business. It's a diary entry.

My process for every insider sale, and it's boring on purpose. Count the shares sold. Count the shares still held. Divide. Then check: was it a plan, and when was it set? Four steps. An insider sale is a number you divide, not a headline you read. Don't guess. Measure.

Now the fun part. Watch what the share did on Friday 25 Sep, the day after the filing. Thursday close $120.82. Overnight $121.51. Before the opening bell, $122.65, up 1.51%, the strongest riser on the Newsroom watchlist. No news. No new filing. Just a bounce.

Then real volume arrived. By the 14:30 UK edition it was $120.30, down 0.43%. By 16:30 UK, $118.68, down 1.77%, with a session low of $117.53. That's 3.24% below the pre-market mark. Company documents filed in that window: none. The newest filing was still the Form 4 from 24 Sep.

So what moved it? Not the boss. His prints were $125.33 and $126.14 on 22 Sep, above Thursday's close. Not a document. Nothing new was lodged. A share that swings 3.24% on no company news is being moved by who is trading it, not by what the business is worth.

Could I be wrong? Of course. I don't know where $HOOD opens on Monday. Nobody does. What I do know is which numbers carry information and which are noise. A pre-market pop with no document behind it is noise until the regular session confirms it.

What actually changes this business is its own quarterly results, not Friday's tape. Insider sale: divide, don't read. Pre-market pop: don't believe it until real volume shows up. Not advice, not a view on the stock. Full edition, every source, on the BuyTrigger Newsroom.
